svg.title: One core, seven language surfaces
svg.desc: Diplomat turns annotations on one Rust core into six generated language surfaces while Rust remains a direct native call.

text.tspan: Annotate the core once; generated naming, bytes, and JSON contracts stay aligned everywhere.

g.title: Rust core
g.desc: Schematics, fields, and simulation live here once.

g.title: Annotations
g.desc: Attributes mark what may cross the language boundary.

g.title: Diplomat
g.desc: Contracts become stable names, byte layouts, and JSON shapes.

g.title: JavaScript / TypeScript
g.desc: WebAssembly module and typed package surface

g.title: Python
g.desc: Native module with shared naming and conversions

g.title: Kotlin / JVM
g.desc: JVM surface over the stable generated ABI

g.title: PHP
g.desc: FFI package generated from the same annotations

g.title: C
g.desc: Portable headers and stable ABI naming

g.title: C++
g.desc: Typed wrappers over the generated C contracts

g.title: Rust
g.desc: The native crate calls the core directly; no generated bridge is needed.

text.tspan: Diplomat preserves the contract; each generated package makes it idiomatic.

g.aria-label: The Rust core exposes an annotated language boundary.
Diplomat reads the bridge annotations and generates contracts.
Diplomat generates the JavaScript / TypeScript surface.
Diplomat generates the Kotlin / JVM surface.
Diplomat generates the six language surfaces shown below.
Rust callers use the native crate directly without a generated bridge.
